key_insight: A neural-operator surrogate combined with reduced-order latent models can approximate transient CFD for an SMR helical coil steam generator, with different architectures excelling at different flow-resolution goals.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster thermal-hydraulic prediction for digital twins in small modular reactors, supporting real-time monitoring and design decisions without full CFD cost.
method: Built ROM encoders for CFD data: MLP autoencoder for unstructured meshes and convolutional autoencoder for structured meshes.
Coupled the latent spaces with DeepONet to form L-DeepONet; compared against Fourier Neural Operator (FNO).
Added a multi-scale strategy to reduce spectral bias and better capture Kármán vortex street dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that multi-scale L-DeepONet captured instantaneous periodic vortex dynamics in velocity and pressure, while FNO variants were more reliable for mean flow and pressure-drop prediction.
watch_item: Performance appears architecture- and data-type-dependent, so selecting the wrong surrogate for a DT objective could miss either transient vortex details or accurate mean-flow/pressure-drop behavior.
paper_title: Neural Operator-Based Surrogate Model for CFD:Helical Coil Steam Generator in Small Modular Reactor
